Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh faces a tough challenge, trailing by 211 runs and needing to overcome this deficit to set a competitive target in the fourth innings. Shadman and Anamul are set to open for Bangladesh, while Asitha will bowl the first over. Bangladesh will need to bat brilliantly to get back into the game. Let's see how their opening pair fares against the host's bowling attack
...THIRD INNINGS...

Sri Lanka lost the middle order with very little contribution but Kamindu Mendis and Kusal Mendis joined hands to get the innings back on track. Kamindu Mendis fell to Nayeem Hasan after his little cameo of 33 runs but Kusal Mendis held fort from one end and played wonderfully to get his team's lead over 200. Bangladesh will be happy with how they have performed however, they are still well behind in the game. They need a good start, they need their openers to see off the session without losing their wickets. The pitch is not easy, Sri Lanka will come hard as they have momentum on their side. Stay tuned for the third innings.

So, Sri Lanka take a massive lead of 211 runs. They have one man to thank, the top order played a huge part but it was Kusal Mendis' innings that separated the two teams right now. Sri Lanka were coming into Day 3 with a lot of comfort. They had set, Pathum Nissanka batting unbeaten on 146 and plenty of batting left to help the cause. He went past his 150 however, once Bangladesh opted for the new ball, they claimed three wickets in the first hour.

The second new ball brought immediate rewards for Bangladesh, as they claimed three quick wickets, including the big scalp of Pathum Nissanka, who fell after a superb 158. Taijul Islam spearheaded the attack, but the hosts still managed to score freely, slightly undermining Bangladesh's efforts. Nahid Rana bowled with great intensity and produced a fiery spell, though he was unfortunate to end up with just one wicket. Nayeem Hasan accounted for the in-form Kamindu Mendis, giving the visitors another boost. Bangladesh will now be eager to wrap up the innings quickly, while Sri Lanka will aim to stretch their lead beyond 200. Join us at 7.10 am GMT for all the exciting action of the afternoon session.

Hello everyone to the action of Day 3 between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. The hosts have started dominantly in this second match. After successfully tumbling out Bangladesh for just 247 runs on a pitch which demanded more runs on it. Sri Lanka’s reply with the bat turned out even more dominating as they cut down the deficit within three sessions which included a fantastic century from Pathum Nissanka who is still unbeaten on 146. The 194-run stand with Dinesh Chandimal just dismantled Bangladesh’s energy on the field.

Bangladesh chopped and changed as they looked for a breakthrough but it arrived in the dying minutes of the day. Before that, they had to chase the game and were not just made to chase the game but the red cherry as well, as Sri Lanka scored more than 100 runs in both sessions. Nayeem Hasan got the big wicket of Dinesh Chandimal but the way Pathum Nissanka is batting, Bangladesh will need something special to get rid of him as the opener is determined to score a double-ton after missing in the first game. It has gotten very dark and the umpires have asked the players to leave. That will be STUMPS! Sri Lanka through and through as we get to the end of Day 2. What a day for the hosts. Bangladesh managed just 27 runs with the two wickets they had and Sri Lankan bowlers did the job quickly. The Lankan batters were watchful at the start of the innings but once they negotiated the first hour, runs started to come. Lahiru Udara played a decent innings of 40 but it was the partnership between Pathum Nissanka and Dinesh Chandimal that cut down the deficit with ease. The 194-run stand saw both the batters score their half-centuries respectively. Bangladesh could only add 27 runs to their overnight total, with a few late blows coming from Taijul Islam. However, they’ll be disappointed with how their bowlers started the day. The pacers struggled to find their rhythm and ended up conceding runs at a steady pace.
